name: marin
description: Open-source framework for the research and development of foundation models.
one_liner: An open recipe book and toolkit for actually training large language models from scratch, with every step and even the failures documented in public.
buyer: Not a product for most people. The audience is AI research labs and well-funded teams training their own models, plus universities teaching how it's really done.
business_use_cases: A research lab reproduces a training run cheaply by starting from Marin's documented recipes instead of guessing.
A university course teaches real model-building using its open experiments and scaling laws.
A team building a domain-specific model (audio, DNA, protein) uses it as the framework instead of writing infrastructure.

money_ideas.idea: The realistic angle is services around it: consulting or training for teams who want to build a small in-house model.

steal_this: Not a weekend business. If you consult on ML infrastructure, learning this deeply lets you sell 'we'll help you train a private model' engagements.
